touches.text: help is defined once, as a root verb in the base shim, and answers exactly as `list` does: `help` is the word people type, `list` the system's word. It is readable cold (no bus, no device woken), so `cairn help` answers when nothing else is up. WHY: "help is specifically an anticipation of the behavior of the other monkeys in my species."

`cairn help` lists [all], then [operator], then [cairn], then every other device alphabetically. [all] is the verbs every device answers because the base shim defines them (help, stop, pause, ...), read from the base shim's verb table, never listed by hand.

Every device has a shim. Each shim is its own process, one per instance, and connects to the bus as a client. WHY: in the bus process, updating one shim meant bringing the whole bus down, and one shim's stall was everyone's. Separate, a shim restarts itself when its own files change, like the ground loop, and the bus stays up.
The shim always starts its device. Nothing else does.

A bare `cairn librarian` never prints URLs. It (1) launches the librarian's shim, which (2) parses the request (nothing) and so (3) launches the librarian and (4) launches a browser pointed at the librarian's chat page. That http request arrives at the web server's shim, which launches the web server, which displays the librarian's page with focus on the chat window. Each part is self-initializing (5.3.5).

base shim: the base class for every shim, customized for the device it interfaces with, internal or external. Carries the panes every device has (2.3.8), the scheduler (5.9), and the [all] verbs (2.4.11.2).
